source.title: Generalization Error for Linear Regression under Distributed Learning
source.authors: Martin Hellkvist; Ayça Özçelikkale; A. Ahlén

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how regularization changes generalization-error peaks in distributed linear regression, using a different setup from the claim's size, epoch, and sample-size sweeps.
record.gate_note: The study varies the allocation of a fixed total of p=150 coefficients between two nodes, not total model size, epochs, or sample size. Its partition-size findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Double-descent results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Total parameter count is fixed at p=150 and n=50 throughout. The only swept axis is how the 150 coefficients are split between two CoCoA nodes. The peak at p1≈50 or 100 is a local-interpolation effect of the partition, not a sweep of model size, epochs or samples. The authors relate it to double-descent analyses ([9], [10]) but present it as an extension to distributed learning, not a test of the curve. The regularization rows (r4–r6) describe damping of this partition-induced peak, not of a double-descent peak along a capacity, epoch or sample axis. So they do not bear on V6 as stated. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that partitioning plays a major role in distributed linear learning's generalization error. Partitions must avoid giving any node a number of unknowns close to the number of observations, since generalization error then explodes while training error matches the centralized solution. Regularization appears only in the numerical section: it damps the peaks at a training-error cost and is not part of the stated conclusion. They also present guidelines for partitioning.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical and numerical study of Gaussian linear regression trained with distributed CoCoA; it does not use the deep-network size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization error depends strongly on the partition p1 (with p2=150-p1); regularization λ changes peak size and training error.

fits_no_version.finding: Two nodes share a fixed p=150 coefficients with n=50 and noise-free data. CoCoA generalization error peaks on the order of 10^5 when either node's pk is near n. Training error stays below 10^-25, while centralized LS gets ≈60. Theory gives infinite expected error for pk in {n-1, n, n+1}.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In distributed linear regression over coefficient partitions, generalization error spikes when any node's local parameter count is near the number of observations, even with fixed total parameters and no label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Ridge λ between 10^-4 and 10^3 damps the partition-induced peaks to 10^4–10^2 but raises training error. Larger λ raises both training and generalization error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization damps, without clearly eliminating, partition-induced generalization peaks in distributed linear regression, at a cost in training fit.

record.peer_reviewed: International Workshop on Signal Processing Advances in Wireless Communications
record.problems: Numerical examples use n=50, p=150, K=2 and N=100 simulations; no error bars are reported. The long-run analysis uses an independence assumption that the authors note does not fully hold in their overparameterized setting. The regularization results do not identify an optimum.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results on the claim's model-size, epoch, or sample-size axes were found. The cited double-descent findings from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: No deep networks and no sweep of model size.
No epoch-wise curve; iterations are shown only not to reduce error once it is large.
No sweep of sample size; n is fixed at 50.
Total capacity is fixed at p=150; there is no sweep of risk across the interpolation point by total capacity.
No label-noise manipulation (wi=0 throughout), no multiple descent, no optimally tuned regularization on a double-descent axis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link and limits_scope label are removed: the peak studied is along a partition axis at fixed total size, which is a related but different construct. The peak appears with zero label noise (wi=0), driven by the divergent inverse-Wishart moment. That could interest V6 if one accepts the partition peak as a double-descent analogue, but that analogy is the authors' framing, not a test. The Figure 1 theory-versus-empirical check at t=1 supports their own Theorem 1 and is not a row on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of total model size in deep networks.
Algorithm iterations are discussed, but no epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curve is tested.
No capacity sweep across model classes; the study varies parameter allocation across nodes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across size, epochs, or sample count.

The study tests regularization's effect on partition-induced peaks, but not label-noise or variance as their cause, multiple/triple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peaks.
No re-counting of complexity by effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: CoCoA (Algorithm 1)
rows.operation_detail: Swept the coefficient partition p1, with p2=150-p1, and measured generalization error after convergence at λ=0.
rows.measure: Generalization error on independently sampled new data
rows.value: A peak on the order of 10^5 when either p1 or p2 approaches n=50; values are not shown on the plot.
rows.uncertainty: N=100 simulations; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.locator: Section V, Figure 2 and accompanying text
rows.note: This is a peak against node-level partition size, not total model size.

rows.subject: CoCoA (Algorithm 1)
rows.operation_detail: Swept the coefficient partition p1 and measured training error after convergence at λ=0.
rows.value: Below 10^-25 across the reported setting, including where generalization error peaks.
rows.uncertainty: N=100 simulations; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.locator: Section V, Figure 2 and accompanying text
rows.note: Reports that the distributed solution fits the training data perfectly, as does centralized least squares.

rows.subject: Centralized least-squares solution, x̂=A+y
rows.operation_detail: Benchmarked centralized least squares against the distributed solution using new data.

conditions.value: distributed comparison when a node's pk is near 50

rows.baseline: Distributed CoCoA peak on the order of 10^5
rows.uncertainty: N=100 simulations; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.locator: Section V, Figure 2 and accompanying text
rows.note: Comparator result; the study says the centralized solution fits the new data well.
rows.check: This is a benchmark comparator (centralized LS, error ≈60), not a result on any version. It is fine as context.

rows.subject: CoCoA (Algorithm 1)
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the partition-size simulations with nonzero regularization λ.
rows.baseline: With λ=0, peak on the order of 10^5
rows.value: Regularization dampens the peaks to between 10^4 and 10^2.
rows.uncertainty: N=100 simulations; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.note: The text reports dampening, not elimination; it does not identify these values as optimally tuned.
rows.check: Unlinked from V6. The peak being damped is the partition-induced peak (p1 near 50 or 100 at fixed p=150), not a double-descent peak along size, epochs or samples. The state is partial for the damping itself, from ~10^5 to 10^4–10^2; no λ is identified as optimal.

rows.subject: CoCoA (Algorithm 1)
rows.operation_detail: Increased regularization in the same simulations.
rows.value: Training error starts to grow as λ increases beyond 10^-4.
rows.uncertainty: N=100 simulations; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.note: The text does not give a numerical training-error value for this range.
rows.check: Unlinked from V6. The row reports training error rising with λ, which is a cost of regularization, not a measure of a double-descent peak. No numeric value is given.

rows.subject: CoCoA (Algorithm 1)
rows.operation_detail: Ran the same simulations with λ=10^3.
rows.measure: Training error relative to generalization error
rows.value: Training error is on the same level as generalization error.
rows.uncertainty: N=100 simulations; no error bar or other uncertainty measure stated.
rows.note: The text says further increases in λ increase both training and generalization error.
rows.check: Unlinked from V6. The row compares training error with generalization error at λ=10^3 and is not a peak measure for any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Regularized CoCoA with λ between 10^-4 and 10^3, for partitions near p1=50 or 100
reader_labels.reason: Regularization dampens the reported peaks but they remain large, and increasing λ raises training error; the study does not show that optimally tuned regularization removes the peaks (r4-r6).
